description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed verbatim by JSON: "B,C,D proceed."). Probe evidence: JSON session scratchpad jsonenc/.

Defect: a clause matching "" against a walked binary (defp walk(start, "", acc)) forces the rest binary to be built every step: a rest <= 64 bytes is copied into a new inline bitstring, a longer one gets a new view; native also allocates a 16 B constant for "" on every test. <<>> is the same match and costs neither.

Evidence: replacing "" with <<>> at lib/json.fz:239 alone took the strings encode from 551k bitstrings / 15.3 MB to 60k / 1.2 MB, docs from 366k to 171k bitstrings, about -27% cycles. "" patterns are common in lib (json.fz, string.fz, utf8.fz, option_parser.fz).

Done when: "" and <<>> lower identically on all three paths; a fixture counts allocations for both forms; no lib source edit is needed.

Scope widened 2026-11-17 by the builder (JSON), the root fix covering the approved case: in src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs, Pattern::Binary(bytes) asks the same questions as a bitstring of one literal segment (an exact size test plus integer-field compares at the cursor, no whole-value equality). Covers every binary literal in pattern position, "" included. Measured: the "abc" walk 263 bitstrings / 138 views on run -> 0 / 0; "" 266 / 135 -> 0 / 0 on all three paths. Pins 01164 and 01507 fall by one allocation each. Fixture 01707 renamed a_string_pattern_builds_no_rest.
title: A string literal in a pattern is tested at the cursor, so it builds no rest
